tldr: Across 25 buckets, economic damage to Iran dominates the headline layer — at least 16 buckets lead with 'economy,' 'sanctions,' 'economic toll,' or 'currency plunge' — making the ECONOMIC frame far more conclusory than body text: outlets use verbs like 'admits,' 'backtracks,' and 'collapses' rather than the hedged language bodies employ. The Hormuz military contest and Iran's invisible supreme leader are the second and third headline themes, with the latter generating some of the starkest language in the corpus ('disfigured,' 'demand any sign he's alive').

silences.what_they_covered_instead: No French outlet present in the corpus; France's role as an E3 nuclear-deal negotiator and its stake in European energy flows through Hormuz leave the headline layer without any European continental diplomatic voice.
No Saudi outlet present despite Saudi oil exports running through Hormuz and direct GCC exposure to both Iran's Hormuz leverage and the Banque Misr UAE secondary sanction affecting regional banking.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to pathologize Trump's position with clinical language: 'Hormuz schizophrenia' frames US policy as delusional rather than merely contested — the headline inversion of the dominant US-winning narrative.

Only headline to describe the supreme leader as 'disfigured' — a visceral physical-condition framing of the leadership-absence story that other outlets handle more neutrally ('invisible,' 'absence,' 'prolonged absence').

Only outlet to use 'backtracks' in the headline — framing the Iranian president's economic admission as a credibility reversal rather than a new fact, a moral-accountability angle the rest of the cluster avoids at headline level.

bottom_line: Headline coverage delivers a compressed verdict: Iran's economy is visibly collapsing under sanctions while the war holds at a six-month stalemate, with Iran's unseen supreme leader casting a shadow of political uncertainty over any diplomatic resolution.
